segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [gentle rain pattering on a roof] [softly] Let listening open. Imagine the room is an orchestra warming up beneath a roof of rain.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Find the lowest sound you can hear... a hum, engine, pipe, or distant vibration. Let it be the bass line.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet distant birdsong] Notice a higher sound... a bird, electronic tone, breath, or faint hiss. No need to hold it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Listen for rhythm. Some sounds repeat; others arrive once and leave their chair empty.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Shift to the sound closest to the left... then closest to the right. Let attention move like a microphone on a slow rail.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Hear something in front... then behind... without turning the head or searching hard.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice silence as part of the arrangement. A rest in music is still held by the song.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let every sound play together without choosing a favourite. The orchestra assembles itself and dissolves itself.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] If thought has been narrating, let that inner voice become one more instrument, then return to hearing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes and carry the wide listening field into the next minute.
